# Rewrite README.md for humans, generated by a repo skill

Date: 2026-10-06 · Branch: `feature/rewrite-readme-for-humans` · Status: design record

## 1. Problem and goal

`README.md` is 198 lines of long single paragraphs. The Install step on
configuration alone covers the menu, the documentation provider, API keys,
the secrets file, live probes and global-instruction wiring in one block.
The Usage section is one wall of text that includes a full treatise on
iTerm2 tab titles. Roughly two thirds of the file is shell integration, E2E
testing and iTerm2 verification. A newcomer cannot find how to install,
configure and run one ticket through the lifecycle without reading all of
it.

The user's request, verbatim:

> Create an updated README.md. Like for humans, so don't write a massive
> braindump like there is right now. Just present how to install it, update
> it, configure it. Then explain `omc watch` with its options and that this
> is critical to always run in the background so that the gitnexus and docs
> are kept up to date as well as the build-cache. Then explain
> `omc design|implement|review`. And after that give a brief architectural
> overview with some diagrams of how OMC is designed and how everything
> works together.

And, during the brainstorm:

> And also create a repo local skill for re-generating the README.md... and
> link it at the top of the README to make sure it's not manually edited.

Goal: a README a person reads top to bottom, in the requested order, short
and sectioned, with Mermaid diagrams; the tab-title detail moved to its own
document; a repo-local skill that regenerates the README from the code and
configuration it describes, linked from a banner at the top so nobody edits
the file by hand; guard tests that fail when the README drifts from the CLI
or from the skill.

Success: a newcomer installs, configures, starts `omc watch` and runs one
ticket through design → implement → review from the README alone, and
`just check` stays green.

## 2. Decisions taken during brainstorm

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|----------|--------|
| 1 | **Short and sectioned**: the four requested sections fit in roughly 150–200 lines; short paragraphs plus a command block or option table each | User's seed |
| 2 | The fish/iTerm2 tab-title text moves **verbatim** to `docs/shell-integration.md`; README links to it in one line; the pinned-phrase unit test is retargeted to the new file | User; keeps the regression guard, frees the README |
| 3 | Everything else currently in the README **stays in the README**, reorganized after the requested sections; no `docs/development.md` | User |
| 4 | Diagrams are **Mermaid** | User; GitHub renders it; matches the generated docs under `.omc/docs/gitnexus/docs/` |
| 5 | The Development section describes **how omc is wired into this repo** (each project surface and what it ensures), not `just` recipes | User: "development is done via `omc design\|implement\|review`… Nobody will or should call `just check`" |
| 6 | A **repo-local skill regenerates the README**; a visible banner at the top links it and says the file is not edited by hand | User |
| 7 | The skill lives at `.claude/skills/regenerate-readme/SKILL.md`, one canonical file, no symlink | `.omc/skills/` holds only the stage skills omc's proxies look up by name; there is no generic runner for other project skills there |
| 8 | "Build cache" is described as the mechanism (gitignored build artifacts copied into every worktree by worktrunk, kept warm by `--auto-build`), not coined as a term | No spec or code uses the phrase |
| 9 | Rewrite from scratch against the outline; reorder-and-compress rejected because compressed braindump is still braindump; thin landing page rejected because the generated docs are gitignored and cannot be linked on GitHub | Brainstorm |

## 3. The README

Headings are fixed: `docker/PLUGIN-NOTES.md:533` links to
`README.md#development`, and the guard tests (§6) read the section
structure. Line counts are targets.

**Banner** (3 lines). An HTML comment for agents reading the raw file, then
one visible blockquote: generated by `/regenerate-readme` (linked to the
skill file); do not edit by hand; change the skill or the code it reads and
regenerate.

**Title and pitch** (8 lines). What omc is in two sentences: a small CLI
that prepares worktrees and sessions, and a skills plugin that does the LLM
work inside them. The "Clanker" line stays.

**Install** (25 lines). Three numbered steps with command blocks: install
the CLI with `uv tool install git+https://github.com/chris-husse/oh-my-clanker`;
run `omc configure`; install the plugin per harness as a two-row table.
One sentence that Claude Code users skip step 3 because omc installs and
repairs the plugin itself. One sentence that superpowers is a prerequisite
omc installs for Claude Code and the user installs for Codex. One sentence
on tab titles: on macOS with fish and iTerm2 omc pins each tab's title to
the branch, see `docs/shell-integration.md`. Link to
`docker/PLUGIN-NOTES.md` for the marketplace pitfall.

**Update** (10 lines). `omc update` with a five-item list of what it does
(uv upgrade, GitNexus, behavior layer, plugins, fish hook); `omc version`;
`omc install <path>` as the developer path with the one-line warning that it
re-roots future updates at that checkout; `omc uninstall`.

**Configure** (30 lines). How the menu behaves (Enter edits, Esc goes up,
Ctrl-C abandons, each change saved immediately). A three-row table of the
files: `~/.omc/config.yaml` (LLM), `<repo>/.omc/config.yaml` (worktree
naming, committed), `~/.omc/secrets.yaml` (API keys, mode 0600). A short
list of what is set, using the schema labels: default provider, session
model, documentation provider/backend/model, native notifications, branch
prefix, base branch. The non-interactive form with two `--set` examples. One
paragraph on the API documentation backend: key pasted once, stored in
secrets, validated by a live call before anything is saved. One sentence
each: configure writes the fenced behavior section into the harness's global
instructions file; configure seeds `.omc/config/AGENTS.md` once for project
guidance.

**Keep knowledge fresh with `omc watch`** (45 lines). Opens with the why:
worktrees are snapshots of the primary checkout, code and knowledge
together, so a stale primary means every new worktree starts stale, every
`/omc:explain` answers from old data, and every fresh worktree copies a cold
build cache. Then the rule in bold: run `omc watch` in a terminal in the
primary checkout and leave it running. What a tick does as a five-step list
(fetch; warn and skip when off-branch, dirty or diverged; fast-forward;
refresh the GitNexus index with no LLM cost; optionally regenerate docs, run
the post-watch hook and the build stage). An option table with one row per
flag: `--interval`, `--once`, `--enable-documentation`, `--auto-build`,
`--rebase`, `--reset-gitnexus`, `--clear-mutex`. Three short paragraphs:
safety defaults (never destructive, one instance per primary, Ctrl-C stops
it, no daemon); `omc design` waits for an in-flight tick and prints the
exact `omc watch` command when the snapshot is stale; the
`.omc/hooks/post-watch.sh` extension point. One sentence on
`omc dependency watch` as the sibling for external dependencies.

**The lifecycle: `omc design`, `omc implement`, `omc review`** (55 lines).
A Mermaid flowchart first: ticket or description → `omc design` (worktree,
session, brainstorm, `/omc:design` commits the record) → `/omc:implement` or
`omc implement --claude|--codex` (plan, build, committed unpublished branch)
→ `/omc:audit` or `omc review --claude|--codex` (conformance audit, fixes,
`/omc:finish`) → squashed commit pushed, the user opens the MR. Then one
subsection per command. `omc design`: the three context shapes as a command
block; what the CLI does (probe, slug, worktree, title, seed) one sentence
each; what happens in the session (context, base freshness, primer,
brainstorm); `/omc:design` commits the record; the session stays open.
`omc implement`: requires the committed record, runs in the worktree, a
fresh session named `<slug>-implement`, ends on a committed unpublished
branch; or `/omc:implement` in the design session. `omc review`: same
shape, `<slug>-audit`, audits against the record, fixes, publishes through
`/omc:finish`. One table of shared flags: `--claude | --codex`, `--dry-run`,
`--headless`, `--no-mutex` (design only). Two notes: Codex spells skills
`$omc:…`; Claude sessions resume with `claude --resume <slug>`. Then the
in-session skills with one line each: `/omc:explain`, `/omc:index`,
`/omc:document`, `/omc:explain-dependency`, `/omc:investigate`,
`/omc:rebase-main`, `/omc:check-wt-config`, `/omc:finish`,
`/omc:integrate`.

**How omc is put together** (60 lines). Three Mermaid diagrams, each with a
short paragraph. (1) Component map: the CLI (a uv tool), the skills plugin
(installed by the harness from this repo), the behavior layer (a fenced
section in the harness's global instructions), and the project's own stage
skills and hook under `.omc/`; CLI → `ToolContext` → git, wt, provider CLI,
GitNexus; harness → plugin skills → `omc internal` → CLI. (2) Knowledge
flow: `omc watch` → primary `.gitnexus/` and `.omc/docs/` → worktrunk
`copy-ignored` snapshot into each worktree → `/omc:rebase-main` re-mirror →
`/omc:explain` reads it. (3) The skill-to-CLI contract as a short sequence:
a skill shells out to `omc internal …`, the CLI prints one JSON verdict line
(`OMC_KNOWLEDGE`, `OMC_DESIGN_RECORD`, `OMC_STAGE`, `OMC_REBASE_MAIN`,
`OMC_SQUASH`, `OMC_SLUG`, `OMC_TICKET`; stage, slug, squash and ticket-sync
verdicts are emitted by skills, the rest by the CLI), exit code 0/1/2/3 means
ok/error/refusal/bail.
Closing paragraph: the CLI handles mechanics and calls a model only for the
slug, the documentation provider, `--auto-build` and the sessions it
launches; skills supply judgment, may run git and project commands directly,
and reach the CLI's deterministic operations through `omc internal`;
`ToolContext` is the Python CLI's single subprocess and network boundary;
providers are adapters, adding one is one file. The section points at the Development table for a worked example of
project stage skills instead of repeating it.

**Prerequisites** (10 lines). Unchanged in substance.

**Other commands** (12 lines). A table, one line each, for the commands that
have no section of their own: `version`, `install`, `update`, `uninstall`,
`dependency watch`, `dependency list`, `shell-integration`, `title`,
`aws-credential-process`. The lifecycle and watch commands are not repeated
here; their sections are the reference. (Hardening: grug `80-20` on the
original full quick-reference table, which said everything twice.)

**Notifications** (15 lines). Unchanged in substance.

**Development** (35 lines). One paragraph: omc is developed with omc; keep
`omc watch` running in the primary checkout and start every change with
`omc design "<change>"`; the lifecycle runs this repo's stage skills at the
right moments, so the `just` recipes are called by the agents, never by the
reader. Then the table "How omc is wired into this repo":

| Surface | What it ensures here |
|---|---|
| `.omc/config.yaml` (committed) | Branches are `feature/<slug>`, cut from `main`. |
| `.config/wt.toml` | Faithful worktrees: every gitignored file (`.env`, `.venv`, `.gitnexus/`, `.omc/docs/`) is copied in; submodules and direnv are set up before landing. |
| `.omc/config/AGENTS.md` | The rules every agent follows here: red → green on every change, tests run or fail but never skip, `ToolContext` is the only process boundary, never run `omc install` unasked, README.md is generated. |
| `.omc/skills/check` | The quick gate the implement phase runs constantly: the unit suite. |
| `.omc/skills/build` | The world build inside finish: format check, lint, package build, no tests. |
| `.omc/skills/verify` | The Docker E2E suite inside finish: golden lifecycle path, then variations and smoke in parallel, 300 s per test; the Codex gate only when Codex code changed; provider tokens from the gitignored `.env`. |
| `.omc/skills/review` | The branch diff judged against this repo's load-bearing rules plus omc's grug complexity lens. |
| `.omc/skills/explain-context` | Where this repo's truth lives and in what order, so `/omc:explain` cites the right source. |
| `.gitignore` | `.gitnexus/` and `.omc/docs/` are the knowledge snapshot: machine-local, kept fresh by `omc watch`, never committed. |
| `docs/superpowers/specs/`, `docs/superpowers/plans/` | Every change leaves a dated design record and plan. |

One closing sentence: there is no post-watch hook in this repo, and
`docker/PLUGIN-NOTES.md` holds the harness and E2E evidence.

**Security note** (5 lines) and **License**. Unchanged.

What leaves the README: the two tab-title paragraphs (moved, §4); the `just`
recipes, the golden-path explanation, the variation-writing guide and the
auth table (they remain in the justfile, in `docker/PLUGIN-NOTES.md` and in
the specs); the "Understanding a codebase" heading (its knowledge model goes
into the architecture section, its skills into the lifecycle section).

## 4. `docs/shell-integration.md`

A new file: title, one introductory line, then the two existing README
paragraphs ("Tab titles in iTerm2 (fish)" and "To verify the iTerm2 behavior
natively") moved verbatim. Verbatim matters: all seventeen phrases the
unit test requires, and the absence of the five it forbids, carry over
unchanged. Nothing else moves there.

## 5. The `regenerate-readme` skill

Path: `.claude/skills/regenerate-readme/SKILL.md`, invocable as
`/regenerate-readme` in Claude Code. Codex follows the same file when pointed
at it; a Codex-native entry point is added only once its repo-local skill
path is verified during implementation, never assumed.

The skill is the README specification moved into the repo: §3 of this
record, as instructions. It carries the section order and line budgets, the
three diagrams, the style rules (short, sectioned, tables for options, no
braindump, machine-contract names spelled exactly), the fixed headings, and
for each section the sources of truth to read before writing, so the README
is derived rather than remembered:

| Section | Reads |
|---|---|
| Install, Update, Configure | the parser definitions in `src/omc/cli/__init__.py`; `uv run --frozen omc <cmd> --help`; the field labels in `src/omc/config/schema.py`; `src/omc/installer.py` |
| `omc watch` | the `watch` subparser; the module docstring of `src/omc/watch.py`; `.config/wt.toml` |
| Lifecycle | `src/omc/start.py`, `implement.py`, `review.py`; the frontmatter of `skills/*/SKILL.md` for the in-session skill list |
| Architecture | `src/omc/distribution/AGENTS.md`; `src/omc/toolctx.py`; `src/omc/providers/base.py`; the verdict names in `src/omc/internal.py` |
| Development | `.omc/config.yaml`; `.config/wt.toml`; `.omc/config/AGENTS.md`; every `.omc/skills/*/SKILL.md`; `.gitignore` |

`--frozen` keeps `uv run` from rewriting `uv.lock` in the worktree.

Steps, in order: read the sources; write `README.md` in full; keep the
banner and the link to `docs/shell-integration.md`; run the README guard
tests; show the diff. The skill never commits; the lifecycle does that.

One line is added to `.omc/config/AGENTS.md`: `README.md` is generated;
change the skill or the sources and run `/regenerate-readme`; never
hand-edit. Agents working in this repo are the ones most likely to patch the
README directly.

The first README is produced by following the skill. That is the proof the
skill works, and it means the README is the skill's first output rather than
a hand-written file the skill later has to match.

## 6. Testing

Red → green for each, per `.omc/config/AGENTS.md`. All live in
`tests/unit/test_cli.py` next to the existing README test.

1. `test_readme_documents_every_user_facing_title_surface` is retargeted to
   `docs/shell-integration.md` and renamed accordingly. Red: the file does
   not exist. The forbidden-phrase assertions move with it.
2. README documents every `omc watch` flag: build the CLI parser, collect
   the `watch` subparser's option strings, assert each appears as a table
   row (`| \`--flag` …) in the README. Red: the current README has no
   option table. Fails the moment a watch flag is added without
   documentation.
3. README links to `docs/shell-integration.md`. Red: no such link today.
4. README opens with the banner, and the skill path the banner names exists
   on disk. Red: no banner, no skill.
5. Every `## ` heading in README appears in the skill file, so the outline
   in the skill and the file it generates cannot drift apart. Red: no skill.

No test judges prose quality; the review stage and the grug lens do.

## 7. Files touched and non-goals

Touched: `README.md` (rewritten), `docs/shell-integration.md` (new, moved
text), `.claude/skills/regenerate-readme/SKILL.md` (new),
`.omc/config/AGENTS.md` (one line), `.omc/skills/explain-context/SKILL.md`
(two lines: README is generated by the skill, and `docs/shell-integration.md`
is the truth for tab-title behaviour, found during the whole-record explain
pass), `tests/unit/test_cli.py` (one test retargeted, four added).
`docker/PLUGIN-NOTES.md` is untouched: its link to `README.md#development`
stays valid. Nothing under `src/`, `skills/` or the stage skills in
`.omc/skills/`. `.claude/skills/` is tracked by git (only
`.claude/settings.local.json` is ignored, by the user's global ignore), so
the skill travels with the repo and every worktree.

Non-goals: no `docs/development.md`; no changes to CLI help strings even
where README wording would benefit; no edits to the generated docs under
`.omc/docs/` (they regenerate); no badges, screenshots or GIFs; no hook that
regenerates the README automatically (the guard tests catch drift, a person
or agent runs the skill).

## 8. Risks

- **A fact is dropped in the rewrite.** Mitigation: the skill names the
  source for every section, the plan carries a fact-carryover checklist from
  the current README, and tests 2 and 3 guard the two places a reader is
  most likely to be hurt (watch flags, title detail).
- **The skill and the README drift.** Mitigation: test 5 ties headings to
  the skill; the banner and the AGENTS.md line steer edits to the skill.
- **Mermaid does not render somewhere.** Accepted: GitHub and the generated
  docs both use it; a terminal pager shows the source, which is readable.
- **`uv run` in a worktree.** `--frozen` avoids lockfile churn; the skill
  says so, and the `.venv` copied into a worktree may run the primary's
  code, so the skill treats parser source as canonical and `--help` output as
  rendering only.

Auditor: Claude (Fable 5.1), 2026-10-06, via `/omc:audit` on
`feature/rewrite-readme-for-humans` against `origin/main`.

| Severity | Kind | Record section | Location | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Important | record is stale | §3 How omc is put together, closing paragraph | `README.md:239`; `src/omc/watch.py` (auto-build runs the build stage through the default model); `skills/squash/SKILL.md`, `skills/finish/SKILL.md` (skills run git directly) | Record amended: the CLI also calls a model for `--auto-build` and sessions; skills may run git and project commands directly. Contradicts no brainstorm decision. |
| Minor | record is stale | §3 How omc is put together, verdict list | `README.md:237`; `src/omc/distribution/AGENTS.md`; `skills/ticket-sync/SKILL.md` | Record amended to list `OMC_TICKET` and to distinguish CLI-emitted from skill-emitted verdicts. |
| Minor | record is stale | §2 Decision 1 ("roughly 150–200 lines") | `README.md:10-239` | Listed only. §3's own budgets for the four requested sections sum to 225 lines and the README's four sections take exactly 225 (304 total against 316 budgeted). The decision's substance (short, sectioned, one command block or table each) holds; the row is not rewritten. |
| Minor | code deviates | §3 Configure ("two `--set` examples") | `README.md:73` | Listed only. One command carries two `--set` keys, which is what the skill specifies. |

Verified without findings: both tab-title paragraphs are byte-identical to
their `origin/main` README source (§4); the skill is a regular tracked file
at the decided path with no symlink (Decision 7); "build cache" is not
coined (Decision 8); every `watch` parser option has a table row and the
defaults, hook variable, session names and flag scoping match source; the
five guard tests of §6 exist and pass; the touched-file set equals §7.

## Deliberate complexity

None.
